title: The multiplier in the income–expenditure model
caption: How can £50m of investment create £200m of income?
speech: How can fifty million pounds of extra investment create two hundred million pounds of extra income? The income expenditure diagram shows how.

title: Income and planned expenditure
caption: Both axes measure millions of pounds; their scales are equal.
speech: National income and output are on the horizontal axis. Planned aggregate expenditure is on the vertical axis. Both axes measure millions of pounds, using equal scales.

title: A closed economy without government
caption: Assume fixed prices and enough spare capacity for output to rise.
speech: Assume a closed economy without government, fixed prices, and enough spare capacity. Households consume seventy five percent of income. Initially, planned investment is one hundred million pounds.

title: The planned expenditure line
caption: AE₀ = £100m + 0.75Y
speech: Planned expenditure equals consumption plus investment. The line starts at one hundred on the vertical axis. Its slope is the marginal propensity to consume: zero point seven five.

title: The 45° line: expenditure equals output
caption: Every point on the 45° line satisfies AE = Y.
speech: The forty five degree line shows every point where planned expenditure equals output. It is a reference line. Equilibrium occurs where the planned expenditure line crosses it.

title: Initial equilibrium: Y₀ = £400m
caption: £300m of consumption + £100m of investment = £400m of output
speech: Initially, equilibrium income is four hundred million pounds. Consumption is three hundred million, and investment is one hundred million. Planned purchases equal output, so stocks do not change unexpectedly.

title: Extra investment shifts the whole AE line
caption: Investment rises by £50m. The AE line shifts up by £50m.
speech: Now planned investment rises by fifty million pounds. At every income, planned expenditure is fifty million higher. The whole line shifts upward, with the same slope.

title: At the old income, spending exceeds output
caption: At Y = £400m, planned AE = £450m. Stocks fall unexpectedly.
speech: At the old income of four hundred million, buyers now plan to spend four hundred and fifty million. Stocks fall unexpectedly, signalling that firms should increase production.

title: Firms raise output and income
caption: The first response raises output from £400m to £450m.
speech: In this simplified round by round adjustment, firms first raise output to four hundred and fifty million pounds. The additional fifty million of output creates fifty million of income.

title: Extra income creates induced consumption
caption: Extra consumption = 0.75 × £50m = £37.5m
speech: Households spend seventy five percent of the extra income. Consumption rises by thirty seven point five million pounds. Planned expenditure therefore reaches four hundred and eighty seven point five million.

title: Each spending round is smaller
caption: Extra income creates extra spending, then further extra income.
speech: Firms raise output again. The next income increase creates another twenty eight point one two five million of consumption. Each successive round is three quarters of the previous round.

title: Adjustment approaches the new equilibrium
caption: Induced consumption moves the economy along AE₁; it does not shift AE₁ again.
speech: The rounds continue, but saving makes each round smaller. Income and planned expenditure approach the new intersection. Induced consumption is movement along the new expenditure line; it does not shift that line again.

title: New equilibrium: Y₁ = £600m
caption: AE₁ = £150m + 0.75 × £600m = £600m
speech: The new equilibrium is six hundred million pounds. Consumption is four hundred and fifty million, and investment is one hundred and fifty million. Planned expenditure once again equals output.

title: The multiplier is four
caption: k = 1 ÷ (1 − 0.75) = 4; ΔY = 4 × £50m = £200m
speech: The multiplier is one divided by one minus the marginal propensity to consume. That gives four. Fifty million pounds of extra investment therefore raises equilibrium income by two hundred million pounds.

title: A £50m shift creates a £200m income change
caption: £50m initial investment + £150m induced consumption = £200m extra income
speech: Read the diagram carefully. The vertical shift is fifty million pounds. The horizontal change in equilibrium income is two hundred million. The total includes the initial investment plus one hundred and fifty million of induced consumption.
